0.original: Y'shtola is staring off into the distance, lost in thought.

27.original: With the chat mode in <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Say<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>, enter “allin tuta” to greet the residents of Slitherbough.

49.original: I am not indifferent to Thancred's troubles. Nevertheless, I will not apologize for holding him to a higher standard after all these years. He has ever been a man of considerable resolve, and that is what I will continue to expect.

50.original: Though it heartens me to know that some of us remain ourselves in spite of our present circumstances.

51.original: I can but imagine how Alisaie and Alphinaud have changed since arriving here in the First.

53.original: Change is part of life. We can but hope it's change for the better.

54.original: Perhaps you should be concerned with how <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103> have changed.

55.original: <sigh> You're right. And after my untoward remarks to Thancred, no doubt he thinks I changed for the worst. I will have to speak with him later.

56.original: I realize I am not as I was on the Source, but I cannot say I regret the decisions that allowed me to come this far.

57.original: Ahem. Returning to the matter at hand─I really must begin work on deciphering this tablet. In the meantime, perhaps you should take a look about Slitherbough.

58.original: If there is anything you need, pray speak with Runar at the plaza.

59.original: I have instructed Runar to help you with anything you should require.

60.original: Welcome, friend. Welcome! My apologies for our less-than-hospitable greeting earlier.

61.original: Tell me, what is your name? From where do you hail?

62.original: From the Crystarium! I see. And this tablet you've brought may help us find the Lightwarden here in Rak'tika?

63.original: Well, you are welcome to stay with us for as long as you need. Come, let me show you around.

64.original: Would it be all right if I joined you?

65.original: Of course, of course. Anything for the guests of our dear Master Matoya.

66.original: Thank you. She means a great deal to the Night's Blessed, doesn't she?

67.original: If not for her, we may have all perished in the great fire.

68.original: With our priests slain and our home in ruins, we were at the mercy of the sin eaters.

69.original: It was she who drove them back. And with her sage guidance, we were able to rebuild.

70.original: Before long she became a central figure in our community─a great oak within whose shadow many have come to find solace.

71.original: That is not to say there were not those hesitant to grant an outsider such authority, myself included.

72.original: Perhaps it is the smile in her eyes when she speaks of the sunless sea. I feel...whole again, now that she is with us, and I have no doubt the others feel the same.

73.original: She is as much a part of the Night's Blessed as any of us, and we are grateful for all she does in service to the Dark.

74.original: But you did not hear this from me, yes?

75.original: Now, you should know there are certain customs we ask guests to adhere to so long as they reside within Slitherbough.

76.original: To show reverence to the Dark?

77.original: In a word, yes. But fear not, it is not too involved.

78.original: Let us begin with something simple. Follow me.

79.original: I thought Master Matoya kept her room dark because she didn't need the light, but they're all like hers, aren't they...

80.original: Should you see any of our people come to this chamber, they have likely returned from a journey beyond the borders of Rak'tika.

81.original: We use the water stored here to cleanse ourselves of the Light's impurity.

82.original: A simple and perhaps peculiar custom, but it is one of our most important.

83.original: Would you two <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>kneel<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> for just a moment, that I might rid you of the Light's impurity?

84.original: We mustn't be rude to our hosts.

85.original: Please, this will only take a moment.

86.original: This will only take a moment, I promise.

87.original: As Runar lightly sprays you with water, your skin begins to tingle.

88.original: And with that, you have been cleansed of the Light's blighted touch. How do you feel?

89.original: I'm not sure, to be honest. Not refreshed, exactly, but I do feel different.

90.original: Has this water been treated in some way?

91.original: Only blessed by our priests. They are practiced in the arcane arts. As such, it is said their prayers imbue the water with a faint dark energy.

92.original: A prickling sensation? No one has ever spoken of such a reaction before.

93.original: I wouldn't say it was an unpleasant sensation, but I too felt something strange.

94.original: Hmmm. The dark aspect of this water should have no discernible effect. Unless...

95.original: By the gods! Master Matoya was right─you <hex:021A020203>are<hex:021A020103> sin eaters!

96.original: I jest, I jest. What you felt was likely no more than the chill of the water.

97.original: Perhaps now would be a good time for you to acquaint yourselves with the people of Slitherbough.

98.original: For that, I must teach you a customary greeting.

99.original: Allin tuta. In the language of Ronka, it is one of several ways one might say “good evening.”

100.original: The world is not as safe as it once was, and this greeting lets us quickly discern friend from foe.

101.original: Is there a handshake or gesture we should know too? I would hate to offend anyone.

102.original: You need not worry. Merely speak the words “allin tuta,” and they will know you as friends of the Blessed.

103.original: I will await your return here. Now go. They are like to be heartened by your knowledge of our ways.

104.original: With the chat mode in <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Say<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>, enter “allin tuta” to greet the villagers of Slitherbough.

105.original: No need to be shy, my friend. The Blessed are a warm and welcoming people.

112.original: Ah, a newly come traveler. Allin chi'si, and welcome to Slitherbough.

113.original: You must forgive us if we seem strangely reserved. We are a quiet and taciturn people.

114.original: Silent and serene as the sunless sea. The quiet makes it easy to discern the presence of eaters and other dangers here in the woods.

115.original: Tread lightly friend, and may the shadows keep you.

117.original: Allin chi'si. Welcome, friend. I take it you will remain in these woods for some time, yes?

118.original: Be wary of these woods, you will find poison in near everything you see. But fear not─our medicinal tea will keep you healthy. Ask and it is yours.

119.original: You are more than welcome to our medicines, friend. You need only ask.

120.original: I hope your stroll about Slitherbough proved enlightening.

121.original: Everyone was so kind and gracious...

122.original: I was nervous at first, but already I'm starting to feel at home.

123.original: There is still much I have to learn about the Night's Blessed, but their faith and strength of will is nothing short of inspiring.

124.original: I can see now how they've built such a thriving community...
